cases.mapped_repair: An unawaited Locator.fill() is awaited before the password-change submit helper runs.
source_context: parent spec lines 20-24 show the floating fill immediately followed by the submit helper
the fix commit also changes password policy and fixtures; only the fill-await slice is admitted
cases.limit: The Promise-ordering defect is source-backed, but no historical race was reproduced and the mixed commit does not prove the whole test clean.

cases.mapped_repair: A discarded isDisabled() boolean, the only purported postcondition for the one-payment-app scenario, becomes checked/unchecked assertions on the two payment switches.
source_context: parent spec title at line 276 promises that only one payment app can be enabled
parent spec lines 313-317 click PayPal then discard Stripe isDisabled() without any meaningful outcome assertion
fix spec lines 315-318 assert PayPal checked and Stripe unchecked
cases.limit: The AFTER proves activation exclusivity, not the narrower UI-disabled property suggested by the discarded call. No runtime failure was reproduced; other changes in the commit are excluded.

cases.mapped_repair: After Close Preview is clicked, a one-shot host preview-token revoked count becomes a bounded expect.poll() wait on the same counter.
source_context: parent e2e spec lines 31-41 click Close Preview and immediately read host preview-token counters
parent src/renderer/App.tsx lines 751-756 awaits revokePreviewToken inside the async close callback
parent real_client_e2e_host_test.go lines 275-284 increment the revoked counter after the revoke call, and lines 561-566 expose the counter
cases.limit: Only the revoked count has source-backed post-click timing risk. The issued count is already gated by PreviewPanel/Close Preview visibility and is not counted as a second finding. The host counters are cumulative, so this is a timing repair, not exact-token attribution. No historical flake was reproduced; the large commit has unrelated changes.
